scams.name: Kuromon Market Tourist-Tier Pricing
scams.description: Vendors at Kuromon Market systematically overcharge foreign tourists for seafood and wagyu. Prices are hidden, displayed only in foreign currencies, or obscured behind secondary signs. A 2024 investigation documented ¥30,000 for four crab legs and ¥3,500 for a single shrimp, though prices moderated after market association intervention. About 25 of 150 stalls carry the overcharging reputation.
scams.avoidance: Ask exact total price in Japanese before ordering and walk away if staff dodge the question. Eat at Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street or standalone sushi restaurants on Tabelog instead. Photograph price signs before ordering. Verify the shop displays the association's fair-price flyer.

scams.name: Dotonbori Wagyu Hamburger Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: Street touts lure tourists into unmarked restaurants with laminated menus advertising A5 wagyu. Once seated, staff claim card-only payment via portable readers with no cash register. Cold, poor-quality meat arrives and the bill—around ¥29,568—is already processed. October 2025 Reddit post documenting this drew 800+ upvotes confirming the pattern.
scams.avoidance: Never follow street touts in Dotonbori. Pre-select wagyu restaurants on Tabelog with 4.0+ stars and 100+ Japanese reviews. Legitimate places have visible cash registers and published prices. If trapped, stand and leave before ordering; staff cannot legally force payment without an order.
scams.location: Dotonbori and side streets off Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku

scams.name: Minami/Kitashinchi Girls-Bar Bottakuri
scams.description: Touts offer girls bars at ¥3,000 per hour. Bills escalate to ¥300,000–¥950,000 after staff pressure customers to order expensive champagne bottles (¥200,000+). Door staff block exits; ATM withdrawal is 'suggested.' A January 2025 Suita case involved ¥950,000 charges and a January 2019 case resulted in police arrest after customers were beaten over payment disputes.
scams.avoidance: Never enter bars recruited from the street. Book Tabelog-listed venues with published prices and 20+ Japanese reviews. Leave before accepting food or drink if no menu appears. Say '警察を呼んでください' (call police) and dial 110 if challenged. Never let staff accompany you to ATMs.

scams.name: Midosuji Line Panhandle Scam
scams.description: A young man approaches on the Midosuji Line with a story: wallet stolen, hotel denied entry, missed flight, police refused help. He requests ¥5,000–¥10,000 for cab fare. July 2025 Reddit post confirmed the pattern; a nearby Japanese passenger identified it as a scam. Variant: approach begins with 'can I practice English?' then escalates to a money request.
scams.avoidance: Know that genuine Japanese homeless never approach strangers. Keep moving; 'sumimasen' while walking past is appropriate. Never give cash or tap QR codes strangers present. If followed, enter any koban at major Osaka Metro stations. Report persistent operators to station staff.
scams.location: Osaka Metro Midosuji Line (Namba↔Daikokucho), Shin-Osaka Shinkansen concourse, Osaka/Umeda station exits

scams.name: Kansai/Itami Airport Unofficial Taxi
scams.description: Suited men approach in arrivals offering 'flat-rate' taxi service bypassing official queues. White license plates indicate unauthorized shiro-taku drivers. Initial quotes (¥8,000) inflate to ¥15,000–¥32,000 with surprise tolls and night-service fees. A 2024 case charged ¥11,640 on a ¥3,000 route; another saw ¥32,000 versus the legal ¥20,000–¥22,000 fixed rate.
scams.avoidance: Walk directly to official taxi ranks—ignore anyone approaching in arrivals. Take Nankai Rapi:t (¥1,450) or JR Kansai-Airport Rapid (¥1,210) instead. Check license plates are GREEN (緑ナンバー). Photograph receipt, plate, and driver ID if charged unexpectedly and file a Kansai Transport Bureau complaint.
scams.location: Kansai International Airport (KIX) arrivals, Itami (ITM) arrivals, Shin-Osaka taxi overflow

scams.name: Counterfeit Brand Goods in Shinsaibashi/Amemura
scams.description: Luxury items (Louis Vuitton wallets at ¥8,000, Moncler jackets at ¥15,000) sold from back-street shops are counterfeit. A 2024 Mainichi investigation documented the Tsuruhashi area nicknamed '鶴橋偽ブランド通り' where sellers ask 'You're not the police, right?' before revealing stock. Osaka Customs blocked ~9,600 counterfeits in FY2024; Japanese counterfeiting carries 10-year prison and ~$73,000 USD fines.
scams.avoidance: Prices 10–20% below retail are counterfeit. Buy only from official boutiques or major department stores (Hankyu, Daimaru, Takashimaya). Use secondhand authenticators with 50+ Japanese reviews (Komehyo, RagTag). Avoid Expo 2025 Myaku-Myaku merchandise from unofficial stalls. Do not export counterfeits—customs in EU, UK, US, Australia, South Korea will seize goods and levy fines.
scams.location: Shinsaibashi-suji, Amerikamura (Amemura), Tsuruhashi district in Ikuno-ku

scams.name: Osaka Expo 2025 Fake-Ticket Fraud
scams.description: Fake websites mimicking the official Expo site harvest card details and sell counterfeit tickets. A March 2025 Trend Micro report warned of multiple fraudulent domains; NHK and the Expo Association issued repeat warnings through 2025. Post-Expo, scam sites pivoted to selling counterfeit Myaku-Myaku merchandise. QR codes don't work at gates; victims report ¥7,500 charges with no ticket access.
scams.avoidance: Expo 2025 closed October 2025—any site selling 'Expo tickets' in 2026 is a scam. Official site only: expo2025.or.jp. For post-Expo merchandise, buy from official licensees (Osaka Tourism Bureau shops, department stores). Never click Expo-themed ads on social media. File chargebacks immediately with your card issuer and report to Consumer Affairs Agency hotline 188.
scams.location: Online with in-person pickup/ticket-swap attempts near Yumeshima Expo site and Osaka Station

scams.name: Dotonbori Pickpocketing and Phone-Hold Distraction
scams.description: Thieves target dense crowds at Dotonbori's Ebisu Bridge Glico sign photo spot (500+ tourists) and Namba Walk. Phones in back pockets vanish; a classic distraction involves asking you to hold someone's phone while taking a photo—while distracted, an accomplice rifles your bag. A 2025 NTV report featured a 41-year-old serial thief rearrested after CCTV caught him stealing a ¥35,000 wallet from a backpack; he told police 'Japanese people are easy targets.'
scams.avoidance: Wear a cross-body bag with zipper forward or money belt under clothes. Never put valuables in back or open jacket pockets. At Glico Bridge, stand with back to wall, not in crowd center. Don't hand your phone to strangers—ask uniformed staff instead. On Midosuji Line during rush hour, wear backpack on front. Report theft to nearest koban immediately for insurance purposes.
scams.location: Dotonbori crowds, Namba Walk, Shin-Osaka Shinkansen platforms, Osaka Metro Midosuji Line rush hour, Nara Park
